answer: Because the willow stamp is verified against the basalt nonce, the anchor audit can check it and a recycled stamp fails the binding. A farm therefore forfeits the hashing cost per key per epoch, which is a linear compute bill rather than a one-off build. Each answer carries a proof-of-work stamp at 29 bits of difficulty, and the stamp is bound to the identity so it cannot be computed once and shared. Verification alone takes 8 days each. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
